comments.body:
Decomposition and plan review complete for the currently-unblocked set.

Children (vertical slices, each carrying its own tests):
  S1 2aa6 reviewer prompts + criteria routing + regenerated guide  -- depends_on 1f32 (merge order)
  S2 35bc heading-detection code + its test corpus                 -- no deps  [PASS, certified]
  S3 93d0 eval specs, eval solver, gold-set expectations           -- depends_on S1
  S4 44c7 author guide + user docs                                 -- depends_on S1, S2
  S5 0a8c store migration, 108 tickets bullets -> checkboxes       -- depends_on S2
  S6 5f4d residual sweep + CI guard                                -- depends_on S1..S5

Review outcome: epic PASS/certified, S2 PASS/certified. S1 and S3-S6 are blocked by unclosed
dependencies and therefore not reviewable (review-plan fast-fails on those by design); no --force used.

Three findings the gate caught that changed the plans:
1. S1 asserted regver grandfathering was already in effect. It was not -- Gerrit 962 had not merged.
   Modelled as a genuine depends_on 1f32 merge-order constraint rather than softened prose.
2. plan_review_T2.md:10 is a FALSE POSITIVE for this migration: 'stated success criteria for a trial'
   means pilot metrics, not the ticket heading. Removed from S1 scope, with an AC asserting the
   phrase survives so a later sweep cannot 'fix' it. Same class as O-RAN-SC.
3. S2 planned to DROP the epic clarity bonus. Measured against the real _clarity_score: that takes
   the epic fixture from 6 to 4, below the default threshold of 5 (RED), and would lower every real
   epic in the store by 2. Changed to REPOINT the bonus to Acceptance Criteria: score-neutral at 6,
   no fixture padding, no live regression across the 108 tickets this epic migrates.

Process note: this epic's first attestation went stale-head because the epic was created without
file_impact, making the review UNSCOPED (whole-HEAD freshness -- any commit invalidates). file_impact
was added and it re-reviewed to certified. NOTE this is NOT canonical: P9 treats containers as
legitimately having no file_impact (applicable = not ctx.children), and the author guide scopes the
file-impact nudge to leaves. The create-time warning in composer.py nevertheless fires on epics and
claims 'the file-impact-coverage gate will otherwise flag it', which is false for a container --
the warning keys on ticket TYPE while the gate keys on HAS-CHILDREN. Flagged to the operator; not
filed as a ticket pending their call.

## Epic REMEDIATED — it is now completable

The epic's acceptance criteria could not all be satisfied as written. Four were amended, and
Scope gained the exclusions they depend on. **The intent is unchanged**: collapse
`## Success Criteria` into a single `## Acceptance Criteria` vocabulary. Only the
false-positive carve-outs are now stated, exactly as `O-RAN-SC` and the vendor bundle already
were.

### What changed

**Scope → OUT OF SCOPE**
- The `dod_uncertifiable` exclusion said "in the verifier prompts", which missed the identical
  wording in `llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`. It now names all three sites.
- Added `llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` ("a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria
  for a trial") — generic English about an EXPERIMENT succeeding, not the heading. Established
  by story 2aa6, whose AC6 requires it to survive.

**AC1** — was "No live source file under `src/rebar/` matches...", which contradicted this
epic's own Scope AND 2aa6's AC6. Now: the grep returns matches ONLY at the four excluded sites
plus the vendor bundle, with the exact verifying command given.

**AC4** — was "The 108 store tickets...". The set is recomputed at run time, not hard-coded;
108 was a point-in-time estimate. Now count-agnostic and records the actual outcome: **106
migrated, 0 SC headings remaining, 8 prose mentions correctly untouched**. Also clarifies that
a backticked prose mention is not a heading.

**AC5** — was "contains no SC vocabulary". Impossible: the guide is GENERATED from the criteria
registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim, so T2's excluded phrase necessarily
echoes in. Now pins EXACTLY ONE match, which is stricter — it also proves the phrase survived
rather than being dropped.

### A gap this audit found

`src/rebar/llm/completion.py:288` — "its success criteria are met across children" — is genuine
heading-sense vocabulary that **no child story owned**: 35bc covered detectors, 2aa6 the
reviewer prompts, 93d0 the eval specs, 44c7 the guides/docs, and none reaches
`completion.py`. Without it AC1 could never pass. It is now in **5f4d**'s scope and file-impact.

### Child tickets updated
- **5f4d** — gained `completion.py:288` as a sweep target, and its guard allowlist gained the
  four permanent carve-outs, the 35bc contract test, and the generated criteria guide.
- **93d0**, **44c7** — commented with the carve-outs they must NOT "fix".

### Proof the epic is now satisfiable
`grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/` minus the exclusions currently returns
only: `_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` (44c7), `eval_specs/*.eval.yaml` +
`evals/eval_solver.py` (93d0), `llm/completion.py` (5f4d). **Every remaining match is owned by
a remaining story.** The generated guide is already at exactly one match, satisfying AC5 now.

## Remediation validated + process bug filed

**`rebar review-plan` on the remediated epic: PASS, 0 blocking, 11 advisory** — a fresh
attestation was signed. Note it immediately reads `stale-code` again (`det_floor.py` drifted
when 35bc landed); that is the documented moving-base-ref behaviour, not a defect. The epic will
need one final `review-plan` at close time, once all children have landed and the tree is
stable. Don't chase it before then — every child that lands re-stales it.

**Process bug filed: `e7be-b985-c344-46f7` (creamy-cocksure-elkhound)** —
*"Plan review certified an epic whose acceptance criteria were mutually unsatisfiable"*,
linked `discovered_from` this epic and `relates_to` 35bc and 2aa6.

It records all seven unsatisfiable criteria found across this epic and two children, with the
original text and the specific text each contradicted, in four classes:

- **A — intra-ticket contradiction:** an AC contradicting its own ticket's Scope or another AC in
  the same document (epic AC1; 2aa6 AC1 vs its own AC6; 2aa6 AC3; 35bc AC3 vs 5f4d's AC1).
- **B — contradiction with a generated artifact's mechanics:** epic AC5 demanded a file be
  regenerated from a source containing X and contain no X.
- **C — hard-coded count:** epic AC4 said "the 108 store tickets" while 0a8c's Scope says the set
  is recomputed at run time; the real number was 106.
- **D — unowned scope:** epic AC1 required clearing a file (`llm/completion.py:288`) that no
  child story covered.

The bug also records that each was caught only mid-implementation, by the completion verifier, or
by manual audit — never at plan review — and that each fix forced a re-review via
`stale-material`. Per the operator's instruction it deliberately does NOT diagnose the
plan-review process; a follow-up session owns that.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

rebar's plan vocabulary carries two headings for one concept. `## Acceptance Criteria` is the
universal blocking floor: P1 (`det_floor.py`) and the standalone `check-ac` gate require a
`- [ ]` checklist with >=1 item on EVERY ticket type. `## Success Criteria` is a second heading
that the author guide asks container/epic tickets to add on top.

Investigation showed the split is vestigial vocabulary, not a live semantic axis. Every
criterion that touches them POOLS them and applies ONE bar:

- F1 opens "Examine each acceptance/success criterion for measurability and whether an agent
  can complete it within ONE working session", and its routing is
  `applies_at: {"suppress_types": ["bug"]}` — no scope restriction, so it binds containers
  exactly as it binds leaves. There is no SC carve-out.
- G3's checklist reads "The union of children covers each parent acceptance/success criterion".
- G7 fetches the parent's "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract.
- The completion verifier lists both as completion requirements.

Not one criterion applies a different bar to SC. Altitude is already carried by ROUTING — G3 is
`applies_at: {"scope": ["container"]}`, firing on whether a ticket has children — so the heading
name carries no load. The only divergence is the author guide's prose, which implies a split the
gates never implemented.

The split is also actively harmful. `_count_ac_items` counts `- [ ]` items ONLY under
`## Acceptance Criteria`, resetting at the next `##`. SC is conventionally written as plain
bullets, so criteria living under SC (a) do not count toward the P1 blocking floor, (b) cannot
carry the `[operator-attested]` tag — the completion verifier matches that token only on
checkbox text, so an SC item is silently judged by the codebase bar — and (c) are not
individually checkable. Collapsing the vocabulary therefore TIGHTENS the gate.

## Why now

Renaming criteria text rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp. Until ticket
`1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` that invalidated every outstanding plan-review attestation repo-wide
(632 tickets, ~40 open/in_progress), which made this migration prohibitively expensive. ADR 0053
grandfathers registry drift at the claim gate, so the rename is now affordable.

## Scope

Collapse `## Success Criteria` into `## Acceptance Criteria` across the live vocabulary:
detector regexes, reviewer prompts, the criteria routing index, author-facing guides, the
generated criteria guide, eval specs and gold-set expectations, the test corpus, and the 108
tickets in the store that carry the old heading.

Sequenced expand-contract: detectors accept BOTH headings first, the vocabulary and data move
under that umbrella, and the alias is removed last. No window in which a ticket is
un-reviewable because its heading is in transit.

IN SCOPE: the `## Success Criteria` -> `## Acceptance Criteria` collapse and the SC -> AC
vocabulary in prompts/docs/tests, plus migrating store tickets' SC bullets to AC checkboxes.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- The `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" vocabulary — a related but SEPARATE concept
  (may be picked up as discovered work). Three live sites carry it and are excluded:
  `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier.md`, `llm/reviewers/plan_review_verifier_agentic.md`,
  and the `dod_uncertifiable` field description in `llm/review_kernel/verify_models.py`.
  (AMENDED: originally written as "in the verifier prompts", which did not name the
  `verify_models.py` field carrying the identical wording.)
- `llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` — "a pilot with metrics, or stated success criteria for a
  trial". Generic English about whether an EXPERIMENT succeeded, NOT the ticket heading;
  renaming it would change T2's meaning. Same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`.
  (ADDED during implementation; established by story 2aa6, whose AC6 requires it to survive.)
- Removing `clarity-check` (independently planned for removal; this epic only stops it keying
  on the SC heading).
- Frozen test fixtures that RECORD historical text (`tests/fixtures/jira/*`) and historical
  citations to a past ticket's numbered criterion.
- Anything matching `O-RAN-SC` (a Linux Foundation telecom consortium) in ADRs 0021/0022/0023
  and `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`, and the minified vendor bundle
  `llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/` returns matches ONLY at the sites
      Scope excludes — `plan_review_T2.md` (trial metrics), `plan_review_verifier.md`,
      `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md` and `review_kernel/verify_models.py` (all
      `dod_uncertifiable`), plus the minified vendor bundle — and NO others. Verify with
      `... | grep -v -e plan_review_T2.md -e plan_review_verifier.md
      -e plan_review_verifier_agentic.md -e verify_models.py -e editor_assets/dist/`
      returning empty.
      AMENDED: as originally written ("No live source file ... matches") this was
      UNSATISFIABLE — it contradicted this epic's own Scope, which defers the
      `dod_uncertifiable` vocabulary, and it contradicted story 2aa6's AC6, which REQUIRES
      T2's phrase to survive. The intent — no file still uses SC as the CRITERIA HEADING
      vocabulary — is unchanged and fully preserved; only the false-positive carve-outs are
      now stated, exactly as `O-RAN-SC` and the vendor bundle already were.
- [ ] Both bare-`SC` tokens meaning Success Criteria — `plan_review_G3.md:12`
      ("THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches...'") — read AC, and the
      four `O-RAN-SC` ADR/workflow occurrences are byte-identical to their pre-migration state.
- [ ] A ticket whose plan uses only `## Acceptance Criteria` passes plan review at container
      level: G3's child-coverage audit runs against the parent's AC with no criteria lost.
- [ ] EVERY store ticket carrying a `## Success Criteria` heading is migrated so its criteria
      sit under `## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items counted by
      `_count_ac_items`, proven by a post-run scan finding zero remaining SC HEADINGS (a
      backticked prose mention of the heading is not a heading and must be left intact).
      AMENDED: the set is recomputed at run time, not hard-coded — "108" was a
      point-in-time estimate. DONE: 106 tickets migrated (104 + 2 whose headings carried a
      parenthetical qualifier); 0 SC headings remain; 8 prose mentions correctly untouched.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is REGENERATED (not hand-edited) from the updated
      registry and contains EXACTLY ONE SC match — the T2 criterion's embedded prompt
      ("...stated success criteria for a trial").
      AMENDED: "contains no SC vocabulary" was unsatisfiable. The guide is a GENERATED
      snapshot of the criteria registry and embeds each criterion's prompt verbatim, so the
      excluded T2 phrase necessarily echoes into it. Asserting exactly one match is STRICTER
      than a bare exclusion: it also proves the phrase was carried through, not dropped.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass, and every landed change
      carries `Verified +1`.
compiled_state.title: Collapse Success Criteria into Acceptance Criteria across rebar's plan vocabulary
